newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee-based store weighs rebuilding after riot.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee-based store weighs rebuilding after riot.

text.p: Dollar General Corp. was weighing Monday whether to rebuild a discount store and job training centre that was looted and set on fire after a shooting by police over the weekend.
Damage to the store was extensive, Dollar General spokesman Cabot Pyle said.

The profitable store was one of three where Dollar was operating a grant-funded welfare-to-work training centre in underpriviledged neighbourhoods. Students were provided high school equivalency study and exams as well as computer and life skills training, Pyle said.
"Everybody at a personal level is very disappointed. The store just celebrated its fourth anniversary," Pyle said. "We hope to resolve what we're going to do there in the next couple of weeks."

Nashville police said they were investigating the shooting late Saturday in which an officer stopped a speeding vehicle and struggled with Leon Fisher, 23. Fisher, who was wearing a bullet-proof vest, was shot once in the chest but witness accounts differed on whether he was handcuffed before or after the shooting.
Several residents threw rocks and bottles at police after the incident, and authorities were called back early Sunday when arsonists apparently set the store on fire.
